docs.title: First Printer Setup
docs.text: This guide walks you through adding your first printer to Bambuddy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before adding a printer, ensure:

  • Bambuddy is running (Installation or Docker)
  • Your printer is powered on and connected to your network
  • SD card is inserted in the printer (required for file transfers)
  • Developer Mode is enabled (see guide)
  • You have the IP address, serial number, and access code

SD Card Required

An SD card must be inserted in your printer for Bambuddy to work properly. The SD card is required for file transfers, print uploads, and archiving. Without an SD card, prints cannot be started from Bambuddy and files cannot be transferred to/from the printer.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the Add Printer Dialog
docs.text:
1. Open Bambuddy in your browser
  2. Go to the Printers page
  3. Click the Add Printer button

docs.title: Step 2: Enter Printer Details
docs.text:
Fill in the required information:

Field Description Example Name A friendly name for your printer Workshop X1C IP Address Your printer's local IP address 192.168.1.100 Access Code 8-character code from Developer Mode 12345678 Serial Number Your printer's serial number 01P00A000000001

Finding Serial Number

The serial number format varies by model:

  • X1 Series: Starts with 01S or 01P
  • P1 Series: Starts with 01P
  • A1 Series: Starts with 01A
  • H2 Series: Starts with 03W

docs.title: Step 3: Save and Connect
docs.text:
1. Click Save
  2. Bambuddy will attempt to connect to your printer
  3. Wait for the connection indicator to turn green

docs.title: Verifying Connection
docs.text: A successfully connected printer shows:

docs.title: Green Indicator
docs.text: Connection is active and healthy

docs.title: Live Temperatures
docs.text: Nozzle, bed, and chamber readings update in real-time

docs.title: HMS Status
docs.text: Health Management System shows "OK" (green)

docs.title: Card Elements
docs.text: Element Description Connection indicator Green = connected, Red = disconnected Camera button Open live camera feed Settings button Edit printer settings Temperatures Live nozzle, bed, and chamber temps Progress bar Current print progress (if printing) Layer info Current layer / total layers Time remaining Estimated completion time Filament used Grams consumed this print AMS section Filament slots, humidity, and temperature HMS status Health status indicator

docs.title: Camera Setup
docs.text:
Bambuddy supports live camera streaming:

  1. Click the camera icon on the printer card
  2. A new window opens with the live feed
  3. Toggle between Live stream and Snapshot mode

Camera Requirements

  • Camera must be enabled in your printer settings
  • Requires ffmpeg installed on the Bambuddy server for MJPEG streaming
  • Works over Developer Mode connection

docs.title: Connection Issues?
docs.text: If your printer won't connect:

docs.title: Check These First
docs.text:
1. Is Developer Mode enabled? Re-check that both LAN Only Mode and Developer Mode are enabled
  2. Correct IP address? Verify in printer network settings
  3. Access code fresh? Codes change when Developer Mode is toggled
  4. Same network? Bambuddy server and printer must be on the same LAN
  5. Firewall rules? Ensure ports 8883 (MQTT) and 990 (FTPS) are open

docs.title: Status Indicators
docs.text: Indicator Meaning  Green Connected and communicating  Yellow Connecting or reconnecting  Red Disconnected or error

docs.title: Still Having Issues?
docs.text: See the full Troubleshooting Guide.

docs.title: Adding More Printers
docs.text: Repeat the process to add additional printers. Bambuddy supports unlimited printers - manage your entire print farm from one interface!

docs.title: What Happens Next?
docs.text:
Once your printer is connected, Bambuddy automatically:

  1. Monitors print status in real-time
  2. Archives completed prints with full metadata
  3. Captures camera snapshots on print completion (if enabled)
  4. Tracks statistics for your dashboard

Start a print from Bambu Studio, Handy, or the printer itself - Bambuddy will detect it automatically!

docs.title: Quick Install (Recommended)
docs.text:
The easiest way to install Bambuddy. Interactive scripts that handle everything for you.

Linux macOS Windows 
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maziggy/bambuddy/main/install/install.sh -o install.sh && chmod +x install.sh && ./install.sh

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maziggy/bambuddy/main/install/install.sh -o install.sh && chmod +x install.sh && ./install.sh

Don't use sudo on macOS

Run the script as your normal user — not with sudo. Homebrew refuses to run as root, and a virtual environment created by root can't be managed by the launchd agent (which runs as you). The installer elevates on its own only for the few steps that genuinely need it. On macOS Bambuddy installs to ~/bambuddy by default (no /opt write, so no root needed).

Download the self-contained installer — no Python, Node, Docker, or Git needed on the target machine:

bambuddy-windows-x64-setup.exe

Run it (one-time UAC prompt — admin install). Bambuddy is registered as a Windows service running on http://localhost:8000 and the browser opens automatically when install completes.

Updates: run the newer installer over the existing install — your database and archives in C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\ are preserved.

Full Windows Installer Guide

The script will:

  • Prompt for install path, port, bind address, timezone, and more
  • Detect your package manager and install dependencies
  • Set up Python virtual environment
  • Build the frontend (Node.js 22)
  • Create a systemd/launchd service
  • Start Bambuddy automatically

Supported Systems

  • Debian/Ubuntu (apt) with Python 3.11 or newer available: Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ (the installer adds python3.11 on 22.04), Raspberry Pi OS bookworm+. Debian 11 / Raspberry Pi OS bullseye have no Python 3.11: use Docker.
  • RHEL/Fedora/CentOS (dnf/yum)
  • Arch Linux (pacman)
  • openSUSE (zypper)
  • macOS (Homebrew)
  • Windows 10/11 (PowerShell 5.1+, Git/Python via winget)

Unattended Mode

For automation or CI, use the --yes flag to accept all defaults: 

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maziggy/bambuddy/main/install/install.sh | bash -s -- --yes

Or customize with flags: 

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maziggy/bambuddy/main/install/install.sh | bash -s -- --path /srv/bambuddy --port 3000 --yes

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have:

Requirement Details Python 3.11+ (3.12 or 3.13 recommended) — only needed for manual/native install; Docker doesn't need Python on the host Network Same LAN as your Bambu Lab printer Printer Developer Mode enabled (see guide) SD Card Inserted in the printer (required for file transfers)

SD Card Required

An SD card must be inserted in your printer for Bambuddy to function properly. File transfers, print uploads, and archiving all require the SD card.

Docker Alternative

If you prefer containers, check out the Docker installation guide - it's even simpler!

docs.title: Manual Install
docs.text:
Prefer to do it yourself? Follow these steps.

macOS Ubuntu/Debian 
# Install prerequisites (if needed)
brew install python@3.12

# Clone and setup
git clone https://github.com/maziggy/bambuddy.git
cd bambuddy
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.lock

# Run (--loop asyncio avoids a uvloop TLS bug that can truncate
# Virtual Printer FTP uploads on slow storage — see #1896)
uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --loop asyncio

# Install prerequisites (Ubuntu 22.04, whose python3 is 3.10:
# install python3.11 python3.11-venv and use python3.11 below)
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3 python3-venv python3-pip git

# Clone and setup
git clone https://github.com/maziggy/bambuddy.git
cd bambuddy
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.lock

# Run (--loop asyncio avoids a uvloop TLS bug that can truncate
# Virtual Printer FTP uploads on slow storage — see #1896)
uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --loop asyncio

Open http://localhost:8000 in your browser (substitute your server's hostname or IP if Bambuddy isn't running on the same machine you're browsing from).

docs.title: Running as a Service
docs.text:
For production use, run Bambuddy as a system service that starts automatically.

systemd (Linux) launchd (macOS)

Create the service file:

sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/bambuddy.service

Add this content (adjust paths for your system):

[Unit]
Description=BamBuddy Print Archive
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=YOUR_USERNAME
Group=YOUR_USERNAME
WorkingDirectory=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy
Environment="PATH=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/venv/bin"

# Kill any zombie ffmpeg processes before starting/after stopping
# The - prefix ignores errors if no ffmpeg processes exist
ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/pkill -9 ffmpeg
ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/pkill -9 ffmpeg

# Ensure directories exist and have correct permissions
# The + prefix runs the command as root even though User= is set
ExecStartPre=+/bin/mkdir -p /home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/logs
ExecStartPre=+/bin/mkdir -p /home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/archive
ExecStartPre=+/bin/chown -R YOUR_USERNAME:YOUR_USERNAME /home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/logs
ExecStartPre=+/bin/chown -R YOUR_USERNAME:YOUR_USERNAME /home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/archive

# --loop asyncio required: uvloop can truncate VP FTP uploads on slow storage (#1896)
ExecStart=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/venv/bin/uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --loop asyncio
Restart=always
RestartSec=10

# Required for Virtual Printer mode — see the note below
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Do not drop the AmbientCapabilities line

The Virtual Printer binds ports 990 (FTPS) and 322 (RTSP), both below 1024, which a service running as a normal user is not allowed to do without this capability. Leave it out and Bambuddy itself works fine — but the Virtual Printer's sockets never open, so the slicer never sees the printer, with nothing obvious to point at. The bind failure is a single line in journalctl -u bambuddy.

If you already have a service without it, add the line, then sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart bambuddy.

Why kill ffmpeg?

BamBuddy uses ffmpeg for camera streaming. Sometimes ffmpeg processes can become orphaned when the service restarts. The ExecStartPre and ExecStopPost commands ensure clean restarts.

Enable and start:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable bambuddy
sudo systemctl start bambuddy

Check status:

sudo systemctl status bambuddy

View logs:

sudo journalctl -u bambuddy -f

Create the plist file:

nano ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bambuddy.plist

Add this content:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.bambuddy</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy/venv/bin/uvicorn</string>
        <string>backend.app.main:app</string>
        <string>--host</string>
        <string>0.0.0.0</string>
        <string>--port</string>
        <string>8000</string>
        <!-- the loop asyncio flag below is required: uvloop can truncate VP FTP uploads, #1896 -->
        <string>--loop</string>
        <string>asyncio</string>
    </array>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/bambuddy</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>

Load and start:

launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bambuddy.plist

If the printer is unreachable only when launchd starts Bambuddy

macOS grants Local Network permission to a code signature, and a process started by launchd is judged on its own rather than inheriting the grant of the Terminal that would otherwise lend it one. Homebrew ships Python unsigned on Intel Macs, which leaves nothing for the grant to attach to: connections to the printer are dropped with no error and no permission prompt. The web interface works, the printer stays disconnected, and the connection diagnostic reports every port unreachable while the subnet check passes.

The tell is that running the same command from a Terminal connects immediately. To confirm and repair it:

# Which interpreter macOS actually judges
BASE=$(venv/bin/python3 -c 'import os, sys; print(os.path.realpath(sys._base_executable))')
codesign -dv "$BASE"          # "code object is not signed at all" means this is the problem
codesign --force --sign - "$BASE"
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bambuddy.plist
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.bambuddy.plist

install.sh and install/update_macos.sh do this for you, and the updater re-checks it on every run because brew upgrade python installs a fresh unsigned binary under a new versioned path. Sign only what is unsigned. On Apple Silicon every binary already carries an ad-hoc signature whose identity is a hash of the file itself, so re-signing one rotates that hash and revokes a permission that was working.

On Apple Silicon the same symptom has a different cause and a different fix: the signature is present but its identity changed with the Python upgrade, so macOS sees a new application. Enable it under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure Bambuddy using environment variables or a .env file:

cp .env.example .env
nano .env

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description DEBUG false Enable debug mode (verbose logging) LOG_LEVEL INFO Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR LOG_TO_FILE true Write logs to logs/bambuddy.log

docs.title: Production Settings (default)
docs.text:
• INFO level logging
  • SQLAlchemy and HTTP library noise suppressed
  • Logs written to logs/bambuddy.log (5MB rotating, 3 backups)

docs.title: Development Settings
docs.text:
For debugging, create a .env file:

DEBUG=true
LOG_TO_FILE=true

This enables:

  • DEBUG level logging (very verbose)
  • All SQL queries logged
  • Useful for troubleshooting printer connections

docs.title: Network Requirements
docs.text:
Ensure your firewall allows these connections:

Port Protocol Direction Purpose 8000 HTTP Inbound Bambuddy web interface 8883 MQTT/TLS Outbound Printer communication 990 FTPS Outbound File transfers from printer 2024-2026 TCP Outbound Proprietary slicer ports (A1/P1S)

Accessing from Other Devices

To access Bambuddy from other devices on your network, use your server's IP address instead of localhost. For example: http://192.168.1.100:8000

docs.title: Reverse Proxy
docs.text:
Bambuddy serves plain HTTP on port 8000. Put a reverse proxy in front of it to add HTTPS, a friendly hostname, or to expose it over the internet. This applies equally to the quick-install, manual, and Docker deployments — only the upstream target changes (localhost:8000 for host installs, the container name for Docker Compose).

WebSocket support is required

Real-time printer updates use WebSockets. Any proxy you choose must forward the Upgrade/Connection headers and allow long-lived connections.

Do not proxy FTP, MQTT, SSDP, or bind ports

Nginx and Caddy proxy HTTP(S) only. Virtual Printer's FTP/MQTT/SSDP/bind ports must remain directly reachable on the LAN — see Virtual Printer → Required Ports.

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name bambuddy.yourdomain.com;

    ssl_certificate /path/to/cert.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/key.pem;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

        # WebSocket / long poll timeout
        proxy_read_timeout 86400;
    }
}

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
Caddy is a simpler alternative with automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt. WebSockets and the correct forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, Host) work out of the box — no extra directives required.

Public domain (automatic HTTPS)Local network (self-signed)Docker Compose

/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:

bambuddy.yourdomain.com {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8000
}

Caddy obtains and renews a Let's Encrypt certificate automatically, provided ports 80 and 443 are reachable from the internet and DNS points at your server.

/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:

bambuddy.local {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8000
    tls internal
}

tls internal makes Caddy mint a certificate from its own local CA. Install Caddy's root cert on your clients (caddy trust on the same machine, or copy /var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt to other devices) to avoid browser warnings.

services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    networks:
      - bambuddy_net

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

In the Caddyfile, reference the Bambuddy service by its compose name instead of localhost:

bambuddy.yourdomain.com {
    reverse_proxy bambuddy:8000
}

After editing the Caddyfile, reload without downtime:

sudo systemctl reload caddy
# or, in Docker:
docker compose exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

Large file uploads

If 3MF/G-code uploads time out on slow connections, raise Caddy's request-body limit by adding request_body { max_size 500MB } inside the site block.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
One-time note for 0.2.2.x → 0.2.3

The in-app Update button does not reliably perform this specific migration. Do this one upgrade from the command line using the paths below. Once you're on 0.2.3, the in-app Update button works normally again for all future releases.

docs.title: Recommended: update.sh
docs.text:
sudo /opt/bambuddy/install/update.sh

update.sh stops the service, snapshots the database via the built-in backup API, fast-forwards to origin/main, installs Python dependencies, rebuilds the frontend, and restarts the service. It rolls back automatically if any step fails.

docs.title: Manual update
docs.text:
If you prefer to run the steps yourself:

cd /opt/bambuddy
sudo systemctl stop bambuddy
sudo -u bambuddy git fetch origin
sudo -u bambuddy git reset --hard origin/main
sudo -u bambuddy venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.lock
sudo systemctl start bambuddy

Replace /opt/bambuddy with your install directory if different. Database schema migrations run automatically on startup.

Installed from a GitHub ZIP download?

Those installs have no .git directory and can't use either path above. See UPDATING.md for the backup-and-reinstall procedure.

docs.title: Build Frontend from Source
docs.text:
The repository includes pre-built frontend files. To build from source:

# Install Node.js 18+ first
cd frontend
npm install
npm run build
cd ..

docs.title: Progressive Web App (PWA)
docs.text: Bambuddy can be installed as a PWA for a native app-like experience — full screen, home screen icon, and no browser UI. However, PWA support varies significantly between browsers and platforms.

docs.title: HTTPS Requirement
docs.text:
Chromium Browsers Require HTTPS

Chrome, Edge, and Samsung Internet require a secure connection (HTTPS) to install a PWA. If you access Bambuddy over plain HTTP (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:8000), the install option will not appear in these browsers.

Safari on iOS does not have this restriction — Add to Home Screen works over plain HTTP.

Connection Safari (iOS) Chrome / Edge Firefox https://bambuddy.local Works Works No PWA support http://192.168.1.100:8000 Works Blocked No PWA support http://localhost:8000 Works Works No PWA support

docs.title: Installing on iOS (Safari)
docs.text:
Safari does not show an install prompt — you add the app manually:

  1. Open Bambuddy in Safari (other iOS browsers don't support PWA)
  2. Tap the Share button
  3. Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen
  4. Tap Add to confirm

Safari Only

On iOS, only Safari supports PWA installation. Chrome, Firefox, and other browsers on iOS cannot install PWAs to the home screen.

docs.title: Installing on Android (Chrome / Edge)
docs.text:
The easiest way is the Install app button () in the Bambuddy sidebar footer, next to the GitHub link. It appears automatically once the browser considers the app installable — just tap it and confirm.

Chrome no longer pops up an install banner

Chrome for Android stopped showing an automatic install banner back in Chrome 108. Bambuddy's own Install app button replaces it, so you no longer need to wait for a prompt or hunt through the browser menu.

You can also install from the browser menu:

  1. Open Bambuddy in Chrome or Edge over HTTPS
  2. Tap the menu button
  3. Tap Install app or Add to Home Screen
  4. Tap Install to confirm

If neither the in-app button nor the menu option appears, check that:

  • You are using HTTPS (not plain HTTP)
  • The page has fully loaded
  • You are not in incognito/private mode

docs.title: Installing on Desktop
docs.text:
Browser PWA Support Chrome Yes (HTTPS required) Edge Yes (HTTPS required) Firefox No (removed PWA support) Safari (macOS) No

In Chrome or Edge, click the Install app button () in the Bambuddy sidebar footer, look for the install icon () in the address bar, or go to Menu → Install Bambuddy.

docs.title: Setting Up HTTPS for Local Network
docs.text:
If you want PWA installation in Chrome/Edge, you need HTTPS. Here are your options:

Reverse Proxy (Recommended)TailscaleChrome Flag (Development Only)

Use Caddy or nginx as a reverse proxy with a self-signed or local CA certificate:

# Example Caddy config (automatic self-signed cert)
bambuddy.local:443 {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8000
    tls internal
}

Then access Bambuddy at https://bambuddy.local.

Tailscale provides automatic HTTPS certificates for devices on your tailnet:

  1. Install Tailscale on your Bambuddy server
  2. Enable HTTPS certificates
  3. Access via https://your-machine.your-tailnet.ts.net:8000

For testing purposes only, you can tell Chrome to treat a specific HTTP origin as secure:

  1. Open chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure
  2. Add your Bambuddy URL (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:8000)
  3. Restart Chrome

Not Recommended for Production

This flag lowers browser security. Use only for testing PWA installation on your own network.

docs.title: PWA Feature Comparison
docs.text:
Feature Safari (iOS) Chrome (Android) Chrome (Desktop) Edge (Desktop) Home screen icon Full screen (no browser UI) Works over HTTP In-app Install app button Offline caching Push notifications iOS 16.4+ Background sync

Best Experience

For the best PWA experience on all platforms, set up HTTPS using one of the methods above. This unlocks PWA installation in Chrome and Edge while also securing your connection.

For access outside your home network:

Set up a VPN (like WireGuard or Tailscale) to securely access your home network from anywhere. Tailscale also provides automatic HTTPS certificates which enables PWA installation in Chrome/Edge.

docs.title: Windows Installer
docs.text:
The Windows installer is a self-contained .exe that bundles everything Bambuddy needs: an embedded Python 3.13 distribution, the pre-built React frontend, ffmpeg, and NSSM (the Windows service supervisor). No Python, Node, Docker, Git, or any other runtime is required on the target machine.

It installs Bambuddy as a Windows service running on http://localhost:8000, so the dashboard is always available after a reboot without any manual start.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Latest stable release:

bambuddy-windows-x64-setup.exe

For daily beta builds (newest features, less tested): browse the releases page and pick the most recent prerelease tagged v<version>-daily.<date>.

Windows 10 / 11 x64 only

The installer targets 64-bit Windows 10 and 11. ARM64 (Surface Pro X, Snapdragon) is not currently supported — most Bambuddy deps don't ship ARM64 Windows wheels.

docs.title: SmartScreen Warning on First Run
docs.text:
Until our SignPath OSS code-signing approval lands, the installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen will warn:

Windows protected your PC — Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognised app from starting.

Click More info → Run anyway to proceed. The installer is built in public on GitHub Actions (windows-installer.yml) so you can verify the build provenance directly.

Once signing is wired in, the warning will go away after a short SmartScreen reputation-building period across the first signed releases.

docs.title: Installer Flow
docs.text:
When you run the .exe:

  1. UAC prompt — admin elevation is required because the installer registers a Windows service and writes to C:\Program Files\ and C:\ProgramData\. This is a one-time prompt during install only; normal Bambuddy use doesn't need admin.
  2. License + install directory — defaults to C:\Program Files\Bambuddy\.
  3. Optional firewall rule — checkbox to add a Windows Firewall inbound rule for TCP 8000 so devices on your LAN can reach the dashboard. Default: enabled. Uncheck if you only want loopback access from this machine.
  4. Optional desktop shortcut — default: off.
  5. Install — files copy, Bambuddy service registers and starts.
  6. Browser opens — default browser navigates to http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Installation Layout
docs.text:
C:\Program Files\Bambuddy\        Install root (managed by installer)
├── python\                       Embedded Python 3.13 + venv
├── app\
│   ├── backend\                  Backend source
│   ├── static\                   Frontend bundle (served by FastAPI)
│   └── gcode_viewer\             3D preview iframe assets
├── bin\
│   ├── nssm.exe                  Windows service supervisor
│   ├── ffmpeg.exe                Timelapse / camera processing
│   └── ffprobe.exe
├── service\                      Service install/uninstall scripts
├── bambuddy.ico                  App icon
└── unins000.exe                  Uninstaller

C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\          Data root (preserved on uninstall)
├── data\
│   ├── bambuddy.db               SQLite database
│   ├── archive\                  Archived 3MF files + thumbnails
│   └── plate_calibration\        Plate detection cache
└── logs\
    ├── service-stdout.log        NSSM-captured uvicorn stdout
    ├── service-stderr.log        NSSM-captured uvicorn stderr
    └── *.log                     Bambuddy application logs

The split between Program Files (read-only after install, replaced on update) and ProgramData (persistent user data) means updates never touch your database or archives.

docs.title: Windows Service
docs.text:
Bambuddy runs as a Windows service named Bambuddy, registered to start automatically at boot. The service runs as LocalSystem.

Setting Value Service name Bambuddy Display name Bambuddy Startup type Automatic Account LocalSystem Restart on failure Yes (NSSM-managed, 5s delay)

Why LocalSystem?

The optional Virtual Printer feature needs to bind privileged ports (322 / 990 / 8883) for the RTSPS camera proxy, FTPS file server, and MQTT broker that emulate a real Bambu printer for slicer uploads. Only LocalSystem or a similarly-privileged account can bind ports below 1024 on Windows. If you don't use Virtual Printer mode, the extra privilege isn't doing anything — it's there so you can flip the feature on later without a service-account change.

docs.title: Managing the service
docs.text:
Get-Service Bambuddy            # Status
Start-Service Bambuddy          # Start
Stop-Service Bambuddy           # Stop
Restart-Service Bambuddy        # Restart

Or via the GUI: services.msc → find Bambuddy.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
To update to a new version, just download and run the newer installer over the existing install. Inno Setup detects the prior install, stops the running Bambuddy service, replaces the program files, and re-registers + restarts the service automatically.

  • Your data in C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\ is untouched.
  • Your settings (notifications, integrations, OAuth tokens) persist.
  • The service stops for ~5 seconds during the file swap.
1. Download the new bambuddy-windows-x64-setup.exe
2. Run it (UAC prompt)
3. Click through the wizard (your existing config is detected)
4. Service restarts on the new version automatically

No manual Stop-Service is needed — the installer handles that with a pre-install hook. If you do see a "file in use" error, stop the service manually (Stop-Service Bambuddy in admin PowerShell) and click Retry.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
Standard Windows uninstall flow:

  • Settings → Apps → search "Bambuddy" → Uninstall, or
  • Control Panel → Programs and Features → Bambuddy → Uninstall

The uninstaller stops the service, removes the Windows Firewall rule, deletes the C:\Program Files\Bambuddy\ install tree, and deregisters the service.

Your data is preserved by default

C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\ (database, archives, logs) is not removed by the uninstaller. If you reinstall Bambuddy later, you'll pick up exactly where you left off. To wipe everything, delete the C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\ folder manually after uninstall.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Bambuddy writes three log streams on Windows:

File Source C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\service-stdout.log NSSM-captured uvicorn stdout C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\service-stderr.log NSSM-captured uvicorn stderr + Python tracebacks C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\bambuddy.log Bambuddy's own rotating application log

Quick log access:

# Tail the service stdout
Get-Content "C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\service-stdout.log" -Tail 100 -Wait

# Tail Bambuddy's app log
Get-Content "C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\bambuddy.log" -Tail 100 -Wait

A Start Menu shortcut Bambuddy → Bambuddy Logs opens the logs folder in Explorer for quick triage.

docs.title: :material-firewall: Windows Firewall
docs.text:
If you ticked Add firewall rule during install, an inbound TCP rule is created for port 8000:

Setting Value Name Bambuddy Dashboard Direction Inbound Protocol TCP Port 8000 Action Allow

This makes the dashboard reachable from other devices on your LAN at http://<windows-host-ip>:8000. The uninstaller removes this rule.

Bambuddy is unauthenticated by default

With the firewall rule active, anyone on your LAN can open the Bambuddy dashboard without credentials. Open Settings → Security in the dashboard and enable authentication before relying on LAN access, especially on shared / guest networks.

docs.title: Virtual Printer + Network Interfaces
docs.text:
When you add a Virtual Printer, the Bind Interface dropdown lists every IPv4 address on the Windows host — one entry per address, not per adapter, so a single NIC carrying several addresses offers several bind targets. Extra addresses after an adapter's first are marked [alias]. On Windows you may see entries you don't see on Linux:

  • Ethernet, Wi-Fi — your real LAN adapters
  • vEthernet (WSL), vEthernet (Default Switch) — Hyper-V virtual switches
  • Tailscale — if you have Tailscale installed
  • Bluetooth Network Connection — if active

This is intentional — Bambuddy doesn't filter Windows-specific virtual adapters because some users legitimately want to bind a VP to one (common cases: binding to the Tailscale interface for remote slicing across a tailnet, or to a WSL interface for slicing from Linux tools running inside WSL).

For most users, pick the real LAN adapter that matches the subnet your Bambu printer is on.

Each enabled Virtual Printer needs its own address. Add the extra ones to the adapter you already use, from an Administrator PowerShell:

New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet0" -IPAddress 192.168.1.101 -PrefixLength 24

They persist across reboots, and the dropdown picks them up when the Settings page is reloaded. The Virtual Printer page has the full walkthrough.

Don't reach for extra NICs on the same subnet

Adding a second network adapter instead of a second address works only when that adapter is on its own subnet or VLAN. Several adapters of one machine on one subnet hit ARP flux: route print -4 shows a route per adapter, netstat -a shows every port LISTENING on every IP, and other machines can still reach only one of them. Weak host mode does not help.

docs.title: Installer file-in-use error during update
docs.text:
If you see "permission denied" or "file in use" mid-install when upgrading, the previous Bambuddy service is still holding python.exe or its DLLs. The pre-install hook should stop the service automatically, but if it didn't:

# Admin PowerShell
Stop-Service Bambuddy

Then click Retry in the installer dialog.

docs.title: Service won't start after install
docs.text:
Check the NSSM stderr log first:

Get-Content "C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy\logs\service-stderr.log" -Tail 50

Common causes:

  • Port 8000 already in use by another application. Stop the other app or change Bambuddy's port via env var. (Port change UX is a v1.1 polish item — for now, edit C:\Program Files\Bambuddy\service\install-service.bat and re-run it as admin to re-register the service on a different port.)
  • Antivirus blocking the embedded Python — quarantines python.exe. Add C:\Program Files\Bambuddy\ to your AV's exclusion list.

docs.title: Browser doesn't open at end of install
docs.text: The auto-open is best-effort; if your default-browser config is unusual (e.g. a privacy launcher), it may not fire. Use the Start Menu shortcut Bambuddy → Open Bambuddy Dashboard, or just point any browser at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Virtual Printer dropdown is empty
docs.text: If you see no interfaces when adding a VP: restart the service and refresh the page. On some Windows configurations (heavy firewall / endpoint protection) psutil.net_if_addrs() returns stale data until the next service restart.

docs.title: Removing everything cleanly
docs.text:
# 1. Uninstall via Settings → Apps
# 2. Then wipe persistent data:
Remove-Item "C:\ProgramData\Bambuddy" -Recurse -Force

docs.title: Build From Source
docs.text:
The installer is built in CI from the public GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/windows-installer.yml. Build inputs:

  • installers/windows/build.py — stages embedded Python + deps + frontend + vendored NSSM + ffmpeg
  • installers/windows/bambuddy.iss — Inno Setup compiler script
  • installers/windows/vendor/nssm.exe — vendored NSSM 2.24

To build locally you need Windows 10/11 + Python 3.11+ + Node.js 22 + Inno Setup 6. See installers/windows/README.md for the build steps.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
After install:

  1. Open Bambuddy at http://localhost:8000
  2. Add your first Bambu printer — see First Printer Setup
  3. Optionally enable authentication under Settings → Security

docs.title: Bambuddy Orders
docs.text:
Bambuddy Orders takes the paid orders from your Shopify and Etsy shops, sends what needs printing to Bambuddy's print queue, follows the prints, and reports each order back to the shop as shipped, with its tracking number. From order to parcel, one screen.

It is a separate application from Bambuddy, with a yearly licence. Bambuddy itself stays free and open source; Orders talks to it only through Bambuddy's API.

Try it first

The Bambuddy demo includes Orders with a sample shop: open Orders in the demo's sidebar. Nothing there reaches a real shop, and the demo resets when it ends.

docs.title: How an order flows
docs.text:
1. A buyer pays in your shop. Within about a minute (Etsy: within 5 minutes) the order is in Orders.
  2. Orders looks up the product's setup: which print file, which plate, how many units a plate holds. Items already on your shelf are taken from stock.
  3. The prints go to Bambuddy's queue, as one batch per print file, and Orders shows their progress under In production.
  4. Printed orders wait under To pack with a pick list. You pack them, enter the tracking numbers, and press Ship: the shop marks the order fulfilled and emails the buyer (in Shopify, only if you leave notify on).

Anything Orders can't decide alone (a product without a setup, a personalised item, a failed print) stops under To do, with its fix right there.

docs.title: Your data stays with you
docs.text:
Orders runs on your own server, next to Bambuddy. Your shop credentials stay encrypted in your installation, and Orders stores no buyer names, email or postal addresses: only the order number, the items, the total and the country it ships to.

Etsy is the one exception to "nothing leaves your server": Etsy requires our app's key on every request, so Etsy requests pass through our gateway. It passes them through without storing the orders; see Connecting shops.

docs.title: Plans
docs.text:
Starter Pro Connected shops (Shopify and Etsy together) 2 10 Features all all Billing yearly yearly

A licence runs one Orders installation. Full refund within 14 days of the purchase or of a renewal, no reason needed.

When a licence ends, Orders stops taking in new orders. Orders already in it can still be printed, packed and shipped, and nothing is deleted. Renewing takes in the orders placed in the meantime, as far as the shop still lists them (Shopify: the last 60 days).

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Bambuddy 1.3.0 or newer, reachable from the machine that runs Orders.
  • Docker with Docker Compose v2, on a machine that is always on. The one running Bambuddy is fine. 64-bit PCs (amd64) and Raspberry Pi ⅘ (arm64) both work.
  • A Shopify store you own (or are allowed to develop apps for), and/or an Etsy shop.
  • Your licence key, from the email you got after buying.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Installation: start Orders and activate the licence
  • Connecting shops: Shopify and Etsy
  • Products and stock: tell Orders what to print for each product
  • Daily use: the pages and the settings worth knowing
  • Help and support

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
• Bambuddy Orders terms (Deutsch)
  • Data processing agreement (Deutsch)
  • Privacy policy, section 10

docs.title: Daily use
docs.text: Orders is organised by what happens to an order next. Every order has a ship-by day and turns red when it is late. Clicking an order on any page opens its details: what was paid and where it ships, its items, its prints in Bambuddy and its history.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: What needs you, what is printing, what is ready to pack.

docs.title: To do
docs.text: Orders that need a decision: not set up, personalised, print failed, a Bambuddy error. Each has its fix right there. Finished top-ups wait here under Stock to count.

docs.title: In production
docs.text: Live print progress from Bambuddy.

docs.title: To pack
docs.text:
Printed orders with a pick list and a printable pack list. Tick them, press Ship, choose the carrier and enter the tracking numbers. The shop marks them fulfilled; Shopify emails the buyer if you leave notify on, Etsy always does.

Local pickup orders (Shopify) are marked "Pickup", and "Pay at pickup" while unpaid, and have no Ship button. Ready for pickup tells Shopify, which emails the buyer; the order then waits under "Waiting for pickup" until you press Picked up. A buyer who is already there can be handed the order with Picked up straight away.

docs.title: Shipped
docs.text:
Shipped and cancelled orders with tracking links, for the last 30 days, 90 days, year or any time, searchable by order number, item, SKU or tracking number.

Archive puts a finished order away; Archive old orders does it for every order finished more than 30, 90, 180 or 365 days ago. Archived orders are never deleted: they stay under Archived, searchable, and Bring back returns one.

docs.title: Products and Parts
docs.text: See Products and stock.

docs.title: Settings worth knowing
docs.text:
• Order processing → Send paid orders automatically: off means every order waits in To do until you press Send. Keep it off for your first days, until you trust your setups.
  • Order processing → Start print jobs by hand in Bambuddy: on means the jobs land in Bambuddy's queue staged and wait until someone starts them there; In production shows "Waiting to be started in Bambuddy". Off, the default, starts them as soon as a printer is free.
  • Order processing → Handling time: working days until a Shopify order should ship, which sets its ship-by day. The default is 3; 0 switches it off. Etsy orders use the ship-by date Etsy gives them, from your listings' processing times.
  • Notifications: which events reach your phone through Bambuddy's notification channels: orders that need you, a shop that can't be reached, the daily pack list, new orders. In Bambuddy, switch on Messages from connected apps for those channels.
  • Business details: your logo, business name, website and contact, printed at the head of each parcel's page on the pack list. Leave a field empty to leave it off.

docs.title: Orders inside Bambuddy
docs.text:
Add Orders to Bambuddy's sidebar: in Bambuddy, Settings → Sidebar Links → External links, with Orders' address. Orders then opens inside Bambuddy, and the link shows how many orders and top-ups wait in To do (the API key needs Send notifications).

Note

Open Bambuddy by the same address you entered in Orders' setup. For safety, Orders refuses to be shown inside any other site, so a different host name or IP address leaves the frame empty.

docs.title: Where to ask
docs.text:
• Using Orders, and faults: open an issue at github.com/maziggy/bambuddy/issues and say it is about Bambuddy Orders. Issues are public: never post your licence key, orders or buyer data there.
  • Your licence key, your subscription or a refund: email support@bambuddy.cool, or reply to the email with your key.

What helps us help you:

  1. what you did and what you expected;
  2. what happened instead (a screenshot helps);
  3. for a fault, Settings → Support → Download diagnostics. The file holds your setup and Orders' recent log, but no passwords, keys or buyer data. Have a look before you send it, and send it by email rather than posting it.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• New orders arrive by polling: Shopify within about a minute, Etsy within 5 minutes.
  • A whole order ships at once. Partial shipments are done in Shopify.
  • An order that is partly collected and partly shipped is treated as shipped.
  • An order edited in Shopify while it is printing waits in To do: once printing has started, Orders doesn't add or remove prints in Bambuddy by itself.
  • An Etsy order refunded in part still prints every item: Orders reads an Etsy order's items once.
  • In some regions Etsy only lets partner apps mark orders shipped. There the order says so; mark it shipped on Etsy, and Orders follows.
  • Bambuddy's queue gets one batch per print file per order, so an order with three different items shows up there as three groups. Orders shows them together.

docs.title: Lost the admin password
docs.text:
While you still know it, change it under Settings → Admin password.

If it is lost, set a new one on the server:

docker exec -it bambuddy-orders reset-admin-password

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: About 15 minutes, plus connecting your shops afterwards.

docs.title: 1. Sign in to the image registry
docs.text:
Orders' image comes from registry.bambuddy.cool. Your licence key is the password:

docker login registry.bambuddy.cool -u orders

Paste the licence key when it asks for the password. Docker remembers the login, so this is needed once per machine.

Note

The registry lets you pull for as long as your licence runs. An expired or withdrawn licence gets a message saying so.

docs.title: 2. Start Orders
docs.text:
Make a folder, for example ~/bambuddy-orders, and save this in it as docker-compose.yml:

services:
  bambuddy-orders:
    image: registry.bambuddy.cool/bambuddy-orders:latest
    container_name: bambuddy-orders
    ports:
      - "8090:8090"
    environment:
      # Owner of ./data on the host (run `id` to find yours).
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped

Run id and put your user and group numbers into PUID and PGID if they aren't 1000. Then:

docker compose up -d

docs.title: 3. First setup
docs.text:
Open http://<this machine>:8090. The setup page asks for:

  • an admin password, at least 10 characters. It always works, even when Bambuddy is down. Signed in with it, you stay signed in while you use Orders and are signed out after 7 days without; your browser's password manager can save it.
  • the address of Orders as your browser reaches it, for example http://192.168.1.20:8090.
  • the Bambuddy address, for example http://192.168.1.20:8000.
  • a Bambuddy API key. In Bambuddy, go to Settings → API Keys and create a key with Read Status, Manage Queue and Send notifications ticked. An existing key can't be edited there, so make a new one.
  • optionally, Sign in with Bambuddy, so your team signs in to Orders with their Bambuddy accounts. In Bambuddy, go to Settings → API Keys → Connected Apps, add an app with the callback address Orders shows you, and paste its client ID and secret into Orders. Bambuddy's own login must be on for this.

All of these can be changed later under Settings → Bambuddy. The screenshot comes from the demo, which runs without Bambuddy's login, so its addresses are the demo's and Sign in with Bambuddy is not set up there.

docs.title: 4. Activate the licence
docs.text:
Go to Settings → Licence, paste the key and press Activate.

Until a licence is active, Orders takes in no orders, and a red line on every page says why. A key runs one installation at a time. To move to another machine, press Remove from this install on the old one first, then activate on the new one.

Orders checks the licence about every 6 hours. If our licence server can't be reached, Orders keeps taking in orders for 7 days.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
When a new version is out, the Overview says so, and Settings → Support shows what changed. Check for updates there checks at once. To update, in the folder with your docker-compose.yml:

docker compose pull && docker compose up -d

Not docker compose restart: that keeps the old image. Your data stays in ./data.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: Everything Orders keeps is in ./data. Back up that folder, for example with the rest of your server's backups. Your orders themselves also stay in your shops.

docs.title: Coming from the beta
docs.text: Beta installs pulled ghcr.io/maziggy/bambuddy-orders:beta. Switch to the registry: run the docker login from step 1 with your beta key, change the image: line to registry.bambuddy.cool/bambuddy-orders:latest, and run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d. Your data and setup stay as they are.

docs.title: Products and stock
docs.text: Orders prints an order only when it knows what to print for each item. That is a product's setup, made once per variant under Products.

docs.title: Setting up a product
docs.text:
For each variant you sell, choose:

  • the print file from Bambuddy's library,
  • the plate in it,
  • how many units a plate holds, or how many plates one unit needs.

Files named like the variant's SKU are suggested automatically. Search finds a product by title, variant title or SKU; Products shows 50 at a time.

Products deleted in your shop are listed apart under Removed from shop, where their setups can still be looked at or removed.

docs.title: Items you don't print
docs.text:
• Don't print, set in the product's setup, is for items you never print: stickers, gift cards, items always sold from stock.
  • Don't print for this order, on an order in To do, is for one order whose item you have on hand. The order moves on to To pack; the product is not changed.

Personalised items, and items without a setup, always stop in To do for you.

docs.title: The same product in two shops
docs.text:
A product sold in Shopify and on Etsy is two products in Orders. Link them, and one setup serves both:

  • In a product's setup, Same product in another shop offers the variant with the same SKU first, and a search finds the rest.
  • In a variant not set up yet, Use the setup of ... takes over the setup of its twin, which stays as it is.
  • The suggestions on Products also offer the link when a variant has the SKU of one set up in another shop.

Linked products show as one line with a badge per shop. A change to either is saved for both. A badge's unlink button, or Unlink in the setup, separates them again: the one taken out keeps the setup as its own copy, but not the stock goal.

docs.title: Parts and the shelf
docs.text:
Parts lists the printed parts your products are made of: how many are on the shelf, promised to orders, free and still printing, with corrections, history, and how prints and quality checks went.

Enter your shelf count for a part, and an order the shelf covers goes straight to To pack; only what is missing is printed. A part no product uses any more, with nothing on the shelf, promised or printing, can be archived; it comes back by itself as soon as a product uses it again.

docs.title: Stock goals
docs.text: Give a product a stock goal in its setup (keep at least / top up to). Orders then takes pieces from the shelf first, and top-ups print for the shelf in whole plates. A finished top-up waits in To do under Stock to count until you enter how many passed your quality check. Linked products count a stock goal once.

docs.title: Connecting shops
docs.text:
Orders takes in orders from any number of Shopify stores and Etsy shops at the same time, up to the number your plan includes (Starter 2, Pro 10, both kinds together). Settings → Shops shows how many are connected out of how many.

A disconnected shop keeps its orders and history and frees its place. Connecting a shop beyond your plan is refused with a message saying so; shops already connected are never cut off.

docs.title: Shopify
docs.text:
Shopify no longer lets you create a "custom app" in the store admin (since 1 January 2026). You create one in Shopify's Dev Dashboard instead, and Orders talks to Shopify with that app's client ID and secret. The secret stays on your server.

  1. Open dev.shopify.com/dashboard and sign in with the account that owns your store.
  2. Apps → Create app → Start from Dev Dashboard, name it for example "Bambuddy Orders", Create.

  3. Open the app's Versions page and fill it in:

    • App URL: leave the default.
    • Webhooks API version: the newest.
    • Scopes (Admin API):
      • read_products
      • read_orders
      • read_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders
      • write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders

    Then Release. 4. On the app's overview, Install app (Installs card) → pick your store → Install. 5. Open the app's Settings and copy the Client ID and Client secret. 6. In Orders, go to Settings → Shops, press Add a Shopify store, enter your …myshopify.com address, the client ID and the secret, and press Connect. It should say "Connected to" and your shop's name.

A second store is added the same way, with its own Dev Dashboard app.

Same Shopify organisation

Shopify only hands out a token when the app and the store belong to the same Shopify organisation. If connecting fails with an error about the client or the grant, the store probably sits in another organisation, which is common when an agency or partner account created it. Create the app with the account that owns the store.

Orders reads products and paid orders (and pickup orders the buyer pays for at the counter), and marks orders fulfilled when you ship them or the buyer collects them. New orders arrive within about a minute.

docs.title: Etsy
docs.text:
Etsy needs no app of your own. Activate your licence first: Orders reaches Etsy through our gateway, which holds our Etsy app's key.

  1. In Orders, go to Settings → Shops, press Connect an Etsy shop, then Open Etsy to approve.
  2. A Bambuddy page opens in a new tab and shows the address of your Orders. Check that it is yours and press Continue to Etsy.
  3. Sign in to Etsy with your shop's account and approve. You come back to Settings → Shops, which says the shop is connected. Its listings and orders come in with the next check.

Etsy shares one allowance of requests among all sellers, so Orders checks an Etsy shop for new orders every 5 minutes and its listings every hour. Check now does both at once.

What passes through the gateway. The gateway adds our app's key to each request and passes it on to Etsy, and Etsy's answer back to your Orders. It only allows the requests Orders needs (shop, listings, orders, shipments). Orders pass through without being stored; the gateway only notes which Etsy shop is connected to which licence. Your Etsy access stays encrypted in your installation.

If Etsy stops giving access (you withdrew it on Etsy, or the shop wasn't used for 90 days), Orders says so; press Connect again.

The term "Etsy" is a trademark of Etsy, Inc. This application uses the Etsy API but is not endorsed or certified by Etsy, Inc.
